note: EA-18G with the ALQ-99 pods; the ALQ-249 Next Generation Jammer replaces them from 2024 (MS-9 picks one).

payloads.name: receiver
evidence: AN/ALQ-218 wideband receivers on the wingtips

payloads.name: jammers
payloads.note: the typical three-pod load (two mid-board, one on the centre line); up to five can be hung. The jammer is the payload; each pod it works through is a store (assets/stores/an-alq-99.json), hung by the 'jamming pods' loadout
evidence: up to five ALQ-99 jamming pods

payloads.name: stations
payloads.note: six under the wings, three under the fuselage; the jamming pods hang on them as stores

loadouts.name: jamming pods
loadouts.note: its typical jamming load: an ALQ-99 pod on each mid-board wing station and one on the centre line - 435 kg each, stores like any other: weighed, drawn and dragging on their stations while carried, and vehicles of their own once jettisoned

loadouts.name: self-protection
loadouts.note: the article's 'AIM-120 AMRAAM missiles for self-protection at the two conformal fuselage stations'

loadouts.name: external tanks
loadouts.note: two 480 US gal tanks on the inboard pair, beside the jamming pods: the centre line is left to the low-band pod (ADR-30, MS-7g: a tank's fuel feeds the aircraft's own tanks; jettisoned, it flies on with what is left)
